Section 1 TX Controller The TX transfer switch is designed to operate independently with any standard generator utilizing 2wire start. The transfer switch is programmed locally using the integrated display and touchpad. The TX transfer switch controller, controls all transfer switch operation, generator function, and set-point/timing considerations. The controller: • monitors voltages and frequencies against setpoints • initiates generator function • controls in-phase or time delay transfers • manages generator shutdown • performs exercise operations • logs functions An integrated display is used to change set-point values, perform desired operational changes, and monitor status. Figure 1-1. TX Switch Controller 010636 A simple dry contact (Form C) is provided as a 2-Wire Start (2WS) for generator control. This allows for control of nearly any generator with a simple 2-wire system. An additional communications link is provided for RS-485 communication, allowing external query of transfer switch status and remote voltage and optional power and current monitoring. The automatic transfer switch is used for transferring electrical loads from a normal (utility) power source to a standby (emergency) power source. Such a transfer of electrical loads occurs automatically when the normal power source has failed or is substantially reduced and the standby source voltage and frequency have reached a programmable set-point. The transfer switch prevents electrical feedback between two different power sources (such as the normal and standby sources). Synchronization Limits Synchronization requirements are: • Generator frequency within 1Hz • Voltage within +/- 5% of nominal (based on controller settings). • Phase angle within +/- 10 degrees Voltage Limits The following criteria are used for a local determination of proper Utility. • Dropout — any phase outside -70 to +130% of nominal (not the average voltage). • Pickup — all phases > +75% of nominal (programmable). Phase Rotation Firmware 1.20 and up provides the option to select phase rotation. Diagnostic Repair Manual 3

Section 2 100–400 Amp Contactor Basics Transfer Mechanism • The main contacts are actuated by spring force and a high speed drive motor. Larger amperage units will have two motors and smaller units will have one. • Power to the drive motors comes from the source voltage being transferred to. • Mechanical latch is used for time delay neutral. • When the drive motor rotates it will turn the gears to charge the springs. • Spring tension will draw the mechanism to over-center (Figure 2-8). Transfer Mechanism The transfer mechanism houses the main, current carrying contacts, along with other mechanical and electrical components, required for operating the switch. The main contacts are electrically operated and mechanically latched in place. Power for the operating actuators is taken from the source of supply that the Customer Load is being transferred to. Therefore, transfer to any power source cannot occur unless that power source is available to the switch. Main contacts are actuated by an over center spring linkage charged by a high speed motor. A pair of electric motors charge both Source 1 and Source 2 Main Charge springs at once. If only one spring is depleted, it will only charge that spring after operation. The rotating shaft assembly contains contacts that transfer the load between Source 1 and Source 2. These contacts ensure all phases are actuated together and maintain safe electrical clearances. The use of a duel set of movable contacts allows for some applications with closed transition operation. Transfer Mechanism Operation The primary driver of the mechanism is a spring, which is initially charged by a high speed DC motor pair using a proportional control system allowing consistent operation regardless of system voltage. These motors are used to charge both main operator springs. The charged spring is released by either manual or electrical DC pulse (via solenoid). A solenoid is used to release the latch from either the latched (OFF) position or latched (ON) position, completing the transfer operation. The main charge spring of the mechanism allows consistent opening or closing operation. To manually change the Source Position, first the Main Spring must be charged. The Source state (Open or Closed) and the Spring Charge/Discharged Indicator is on the contactor (E). Once the Spring is charged, pressing either Source 1 or Source 2 Operation button (D) will change that Source State. NOTE: For open transition switches, both Sources must be Open prior to Closing a Source due to mechanical interlock. Section 3 800–1600 Amp TX Contactor Basics Diagnostic Repair Manual 33

Section 4 100–600 Amp TX Transfer Switch Troubleshooting Fault Types When a fault is presented, the Alarm LED on the front panel is illuminated and the Fault Indicator Relay is closed. For all faults, except for Source Miswire and Source Voltage High, the ATS control will continue to attempt all functions while in the Fault Indication State. The system needs to be inspected for proper functionality when this occurs. Faults are displayed on the Warnings screen. Fault can be acknowledgeable (ACKABLE) or unacknowledgeable (UNACKABLE). When a fault is acknowledged (ACKD), it may stay on the screen, but the fault light will turn off and the relay opens. If multiple faults exist, all faults will need to be ACKD in order to clear the fault indication. Faults are removed from the screen if fault conditions are removed. Fault types include: • Acknowledged (ACKD) – The fault is present, the Alarm LED is not lit, and the relay is open. • Acknowledgeable (ACKABLE) – Fault is present and fault is asserted until user acknowledges fault. Once acknowledged, the Alarm LED turns off and the relay opens. • Unacknowledgeable (UNACKABLE) – Fault is displayed and cannot be acknowledged by the user. Appendix A Permissive and Loadshed Functions Permissive and Loadshed functions may be programmed to any available input, but are generally to be used with the B.In 1 or B.In 2, corresponding to J25:1,2 and J25:3,4 respectively. Any of the available inputs may be programmed as Permissive. NOTE: There is no explicit Loadshed function as it is functionally equivalent to Permissive. To activate functionality, the input must be programmed to be associated with the PERMISSIVE function via the MENU - SETTINGS - I/O menu on the controller display. Once the function is associated with an input, transfer out of the primary source will be prevented until the input is asserted. NOTE: The assertion of the input may be made by applying a 12/24 VDC nominal voltage across the optically-isolated inputs J25:1(-) and J25:2(+) and similarly to J25:3(-) and J25:4(+). This assertion is indicated on the display by means of a P with a circle around it (in the top right corner), allowing transfer to continue. The allowable voltage range is 8-35 VDC. The impedance of this input is 16 kOhms, resulting in approximately 1-2 mA of current. Verify appropriate signal relay or external loading is used on a general purpose relay so that minimum relay current requirements are met. If an external voltage supply is not available, an I/O expander module may be used as a voltage source, using J3:1 (+12VDC) and J3:2 (COM). This voltage may be safely looped through the externally supplied signal level dry contacts and brought back to supply the power for any of the available inputs. Note that a maximum of 50mA may be pulled from this supply. As noted in the manual, Loadshed is the de-assertion of the PERMISSIVE input while the switch is in the secondary source. On a 3-position switch, this will initiate a transfer to the OFF position. NOTE: A 2-position switch cannot transfer to a dead source per UL standard requirement and therefore Loadshed is not programmed with any functionality. Figure A-1. 013620 Diagnostic Repair Manual 117
